scenes.tts: A factor lands on the outside of a neuron. How does that switch on a signal inside?
scenes.visual: Title card: Four Factors, Three Kinases. An NGF dimer outside a membrane; a question mark inside the cell.
scenes.narration: A factor lands on the outside of a neuron. How does that switch on a signal inside?

scenes.tts: Start with the receptor. A Track receptor sits in the neuron's membrane.
scenes.caption: Start with the receptor. A Trk receptor sits in the neuron's membrane.
scenes.visual: A single TrkA receptor spans the membrane: binding domains outside, kinase domain inside.
scenes.narration: Start with the receptor. A Trk receptor sits in the neuron's membrane.

scenes.tts: Outside, it binds the factor. Inside, it carries a tyrosine kinase domain.
scenes.visual: Labels: binding domain (outside), kinase domain (inside).
scenes.narration: Outside, it binds the factor. Inside, it carries a tyrosine kinase domain.

scenes.tts: Now the factor. Each neurotrophin is a dimer, so it has two binding faces.
scenes.visual: The NGF dimer rotates to show two identical faces, each highlighted.
scenes.narration: Now the factor. Each neurotrophin is a dimer, so it has two binding faces.

scenes.tts: A dimer has two faces. What can it do to two receptors at once?
scenes.visual: Two TrkA receptors drift apart in the membrane. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: A dimer has two faces. What can it do to two receptors at once?

scenes.tts: It can hold two Track receptors at once, and bring them together.
scenes.caption: It can hold two Trk receptors at once, and bring them together.
scenes.visual: The dimer docks one TrkA on each side, pulling the two receptors together.
scenes.narration: It can hold two Trk receptors at once, and bring them together.

scenes.tts: A crystal structure shows this. One N G F dimer holds two Track A domains, one on each side.
scenes.caption: A crystal structure shows this. One NGF dimer holds two TrkA domains, one on each side.
scenes.visual: Structure view of NGF bound to TrkA domains, one on each side. On screen: PDB 1WWW.
scenes.narration: A crystal structure shows this. One NGF dimer holds two TrkA domains, one on each side.

scenes.tts: Their kinase domains, now side by side, phosphorylate each other on tyrosines.
scenes.visual: Inside the cell, the two kinase domains swing together; phosphate tags pop onto each.
scenes.narration: Their kinase domains, now side by side, phosphorylate each other on tyrosines.

scenes.tts: The phosphorylated tyrosines become docking sites for proteins inside the cell.
scenes.visual: Adaptor proteins dock on the phosphate tags.
scenes.narration: The phosphorylated tyrosines become docking sites for proteins inside the cell.

scenes.tts: They start two survival branches you have met before.
scenes.visual: Two branches grow downward from the receptor pair.
scenes.narration: They start two survival branches you have met before.

scenes.tts: One runs from Ras to E R K.
scenes.caption: One runs from Ras to ERK.
scenes.visual: Left branch lights up: Ras, then a chain to ERK.
scenes.narration: One runs from Ras to ERK.

scenes.tts: The other runs from P I three K to Akt.
scenes.caption: The other runs from PI3K to Akt.
scenes.visual: Right branch lights up: PI3K to Akt. Both branches end at a label: survival.
scenes.narration: The other runs from PI3K to Akt.

scenes.tts: Now back to the first puzzle. How does a neuron know which factor is its own?
scenes.visual: Puzzle 1 card returns: Which factor is mine?
scenes.narration: Now back to the first puzzle. How does a neuron know which factor is its own?

scenes.tts: Each neurotrophin prefers particular Track receptors.
scenes.caption: Each neurotrophin prefers particular Trk receptors.
scenes.visual: The matching table from chapter one returns, row by row.
scenes.narration: Each neurotrophin prefers particular Trk receptors.

scenes.tts: N G F prefers Track A. B D N F and N T four prefer Track B. N T three prefers Track C, and activates Track A and Track B more weakly.
scenes.caption: NGF prefers TrkA. BDNF and NT-4 prefer TrkB. NT-3 prefers TrkC, and activates TrkA and TrkB more weakly.
scenes.visual: Rows highlight in turn: NGF-TrkA; BDNF and NT-4 to TrkB; NT-3 to TrkC, with dashed weaker arrows to TrkA and TrkB.
scenes.narration: NGF prefers TrkA. BDNF and NT-4 prefer TrkB. NT-3 prefers TrkC, and activates TrkA and TrkB more weakly.

scenes.tts: The selective differences lie in a few contact surfaces, such as the factor's amino terminus.
scenes.visual: Close-up on the NGF amino terminus against the receptor domain; the contact patch glows.
scenes.narration: The selective differences lie in a few contact surfaces, such as the factor's amino terminus.

scenes.tts: The overall plan is the same in another pair, N T four with Track B.
scenes.caption: The overall plan is the same in another pair, NT-4 with TrkB.
scenes.visual: Structure view of NT-4 with TrkB beside NGF with TrkA. On screen: PDB 1HCF.
scenes.narration: The overall plan is the same in another pair, NT-4 with TrkB.

scenes.tts: So the answer is this. A neuron answers the factor whose Track receptor it makes.
scenes.caption: So the answer is this. A neuron answers the factor whose Trk receptor it makes.
scenes.visual: Two neurons: one carries TrkA, one carries TrkC.
scenes.narration: So the answer is this. A neuron answers the factor whose Trk receptor it makes.

scenes.tts: A neuron that makes Track A is switched on by N G F.
scenes.caption: A neuron that makes TrkA is switched on by NGF.
scenes.visual: NGF dots arrive; only the TrkA neuron lights up.
scenes.narration: A neuron that makes TrkA is switched on by NGF.

scenes.tts: One that makes Track C is switched on by N T three.
scenes.caption: One that makes TrkC is switched on by NT-3.
scenes.visual: NT-3 dots arrive; the TrkC neuron lights up.
scenes.narration: One that makes TrkC is switched on by NT-3.

scenes.tts: The factor does not know which neuron it is for. The receptor sorts it.
scenes.visual: Factor dots float past both cells; each cell's receptors pick out its own.
scenes.narration: The factor does not know which neuron it is for. The receptor sorts it.

scenes.tts: And p seventy five? It binds N G F at a site different from where Track A binds.
scenes.caption: And p75? It binds NGF at a site different from where TrkA binds.
scenes.visual: Structure view of NGF with p75 lying along one side. On screen: PDB 1SG1.
scenes.narration: And p75? It binds NGF at a site different from where TrkA binds.

scenes.tts: What it does with that binding is the rest of this lesson.
scenes.visual: p75 highlighted, with a question mark beside it.
scenes.narration: What it does with that binding is the rest of this lesson.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: the factor pairs two receptors, and the receptor a neuron makes decides which factor it hears.
scenes.visual: Takeaway on screen: the dimer pairs two Trk receptors; the receptor a neuron makes decides which factor it hears.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: the factor pairs two receptors, and the receptor a neuron makes decides which factor it hears.
